desc: Ideation: reduce problem to ord_M(A)=N via prime p≡1 (mod N) and element x=b^((p-1)/N) of exact order N; only N needs factoring
Prove leftover after trial division of N≤1e9 to 31623 is 1 or prime (no Pollard rho needed)
Identify N=1 edge case (p=2 gives x=0) → special-case output "2 1"
Simplification: (p-1)/N = k exactly, so x = pow(b, k, p) with tiny exponent
Implement sieve of Eratosthenes for primes up to 31623
Implement deterministic Miller-Rabin for 64-bit (bases [2, 325, 9375, 28178, 450775, 9780504, 1795265022]) with small-prime prefilter
Implement distinct-prime-factors(N) via sieve primes; leftover > 1 is prime
Main per-test flow: N==1 → "2 1"; else factor N, search k (parity: N odd → even k only) for prime p=kN+1, scan b=2,3,... for x=pow(b,k,p) with pow(x,N//q,p)!=1 ∀q|N, output "x p"
Fast I/O with sys.stdin.buffer.read and batched output for T up to 1e4
Review final code for correctness and edge cases (N=1, N prime near 1e9, N=2, powers of 2)
